chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the bird owns its wings, so it is for the one who seizes it.
ai.seo_question: Who owns a bird once it has regained control of its wings according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *qabd* (possession) in avian ownership, distinguishing between fully captive birds and those that have regained flight capability. It establishes that ownership transfers to the individual who successfully captures the bird at the moment it becomes free, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on actual control as the determinant of property rights in hunting contexts.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from the one who reported it,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the birds owns its wings, so it is for the one who seizes it’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a bird has full control over its wings (is able to fly) it then belongs to whoever catches it . 555
